title: Guy de Maupassant's birth chart
metaDescription: Guy de Maupassant's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 12.6° Leo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 12.6° Leo, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 12.6° Leo. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Jupiter in the classical scheme — a fire sign read through a fixed season.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 18.0° Leo, Venus was at 21.3° Virgo, Mars was at 18.7° Virgo. Read together: a mind that decides at speaking speed; taste for the substantial and the lasting; drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Uranus and Pluto: 0.5° from an exact conjunction. Two bodies in the same degree are not read as neighbours but as a merger: whatever one wants, the other is already funding. Behind it, Venus conjunction Jupiter at 1.3°, and Venus conjunction Mars at 2.7° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Five planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Leo at 12.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; the Moon in Cancer at 8.7° is in domicile; Venus in Virgo at 21.3° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Jupiter in Virgo at 22.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Aries at 21.0° is in fall. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 fire, 4 earth, 2 water by element and 4 mutable, 3 fixed, 3 cardinal by mode. A fire emphasis is read as appetite for the first move, with information gathered by doing rather than before doing. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Saturn, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde. Uranus changed direction during the day, so its motion is left open.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Cancer for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.9° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 8.7°.
